title.narrative: Green Skills Now Colombia

description.narrative: Children and youth aged 14–30, particularly girls from vulnerable backgrounds in Ecuador and Colombia, including those living in poverty, victims of conflict, LGTBIQ+, Afro-descendant and Indigenous communities, people with disabilities, and migrants. At least 60% of direct beneficiaries will be young women, ensuring gender-transformative impact.

From a financial perspective, SECAP and Colombia Incluyente commit over 20% in-kind support, ensuring continuity beyond project end. Capacity building and curriculum integration guarantee lasting impact so local VET partners can apply the skills and knowledge learnt during the project. From an environmental perspective, activities prioritize climate resilience and low-carbon practices. Furthermore open-source e-learning platforms and Train-the-Trainer models enable scalability. Finally from a social point of view, inclusive beneficiary selection and gender-transformative approaches ensure continued benefits for vulnerable youth, especially girls. Materials will be publicly accessible for replication globally.

If VET institutions in Ecuador and Colombia co-create and implement an Inclusive Green Skills Curriculum, then disadvantaged youth—especially young women—will gain market-relevant green skills, because the curriculum is informed by private sector input, adapted to local contexts, and supported by teacher capacity building. The project engages key actors (VET providers, private sector, civil society, youth) through participatory processes, strengthens institutional frameworks, and promotes gender equality and climate resilience. This leads to improved employability, enhanced institutional performance, and systemic change towards sustainable development.

In Ecuador and Colombia, youth—especially young women—face systemic barriers to accessing quality education and employment in the green economy. Ecuador’s SECAP lacks a green skills curriculum and expert staff, limiting its ability to contribute to national priorities for ecological transition. In Colombia, gender gaps, high youth unemployment (18.5%), and limited access to training persist, particularly in Barranquilla. Both countries struggle with informal employment and insufficient integration of sustainability in vocational education. These gaps hinder socioeconomic development and climate resilience, underscoring the need for inclusive, gender-transformative interventions that link VET systems to labour market demands and environmental priorities.

SUMMARY: Green Skills Now is a two-year programme (2025–2026) implemented in Colombia and Ecuador, aiming to equip disadvantaged youth — particularly young women — with green life skills for the green economy. Funded by the EU Erasmus+ programme and developed in collaboration with partner vocational institutions - SECAP in Ecuador and Colombia Incluyente in Colombia and international technical partners - CINOP and Politeknika Txorierri- the project delivers market-relevant training, promotes youth employment, foster public-private partnerships and strengthens education systems through digital tools and cross-regional exchange. It also works to promote inclusion, gender equality, and climate resilience within the green labour market. By the end of 2026, 150 teachers and 200 young people are trained with green and gender-responsive education that raises awareness about climate change, encourages reflection on environmental impact, and introduces sustainable practices and green entrepreneur.

The project builds on previous initiatives such as the Green Life Skills Curriculum developed by CINOP and Plan International Netherlands, and leverages ongoing efforts like the MANGLAR Environmental Training School in Colombia and Eco-Entrepreneurship projects in Ecuador. It complements EU and national strategies for green transition, circular economy, and gender equality. By integrating lessons learned from consortium partners’ experience in curriculum development, private sector engagement, and youth empowerment, the project fills critical gaps in green skills training and institutional capacity. It introduces innovative methodologies, including design thinking and Train-the-Trainer models, ensuring sustainability and scalability.

Work Package 1: Develop Inclusive Green Skills Curriculum Activities include conducting gender-sensitive market scans and needs analyses to identify green skills gaps, organizing design thinking workshops with stakeholders, and adapting the Green Life Skills Curriculum for SECAP and Colombia Incluyente. The curriculum will integrate modules on environmental sustainability, gender equality, and entrepreneurship. Prototyping and testing will involve 200 youth, ensuring relevance and inclusivity.
Work Package 2: Capacity Building for VET Staff This package focuses on training 150 VET teachers through interactive sessions on gender equality, inclusive education, and innovative pedagogical methods. A Masterclass led by Txorierri will introduce EU best practices in environmental education, while Train-the-Trainer methodology ensures scalability. Teachers will gain skills to deliver the Inclusive Green Skills Curriculum effectively.
Work Package 3: Strengthen Public-Private Partnerships Design thinking workshops will foster collaboration between VET institutions and private sector actors, aligning training with labour market needs. Launch events will promote the Inclusive Green Skills Curriculum, and strategies for internships, mentorships, and job placement platforms will be implemented to support youth employment in green sectors.
Work Package 4: Knowledge Exchange and Dissemination This package promotes EU-LATAM collaboration through webinars, seminars, and dissemination of best practices. Activities include developing a knowledge exchange plan, producing communication materials (guidelines, videos, case studies), and leveraging networks for visibility. Resources will be made publicly available to ensure replication and sustainability.
